Description of your system highlights/te: Our machine translation system combines SMT and NMT to improve both accuracy and fluency. The SMT component provides phrase-based translation, word alignment, terminology consistency, and reliable handling of rare or domain-specific expressions. The NMT component uses an encoder-decoder model with attention to capture context, improve grammar, and generate more natural translations. Input text is preprocessed through tokenization, normalization, truecasing, and subword segmentation. Post-processing restores punctuation, capitalization, and formatting. This hybrid approach balances precision, robustness, and fluency.

Description of your system highlights/te: For the WMT26 General Translation Task (Unconstrained Track), we propose TRIVE (Tri-Fusion Verified Translation Agent), a model-agnostic agentic framework for machine translation consisting of two core stages: multi-strategy fusion generation and automatic verification and correction. In the generation stage, TRIVE employs three complementary translation strategies—Faithful Translation, Fluent Translation, and Free Translation—to produce diverse translation candidates. A fusion decision module then integrates the strengths of these candidates to generate a high-quality translation that balances semantic fidelity, linguistic fluency, and natural expression. In the verification and correction stage, the generated translation is automatically evaluated and refined through a combination of rule-based validation and large language model (LLM)-based assessment, ensuring both structural correctness and overall translation quality. As a model-agnostic framework, TRIVE improves translation quality and output reliability through a closed-loop generate–fuse–verify–correct workflow.

Description of your system highlights/te: Our WMT26 system is a constrained open-weight machine translation system with a total inference-time model size of about 18B parameters. The system consists of a 14B main multilingual translation model and a lightweight 4B post-editing model. We adapted the main model to the 23 submitted language directions and related domains through continued pre-training, followed by supervised fine-tuning with both general multilingual instruction data and translation-focused instruction data.  We further improved the main model with reinforcement learning based on rule-based rewards and LLM-judge feedback, focusing on adequacy, faithfulness, fluency, terminology consistency, and format preservation. We also introduced OPD to maintain general instruction-following ability. At inference time, the 14B model produces the initial translations, and the 4B post-editing model checks and minimally fixes obvious issues such as missing content, mistranslation, formatting errors, unnatural wording, or residual source-language fragments. The combined system remains below the 20B parameter limit.

Description of your system highlights/te: This is a language-specific English–Belarusian translation system based on TranslateGemma 12B, with dictionary augmentation and iterative refinement. The system operates in three stages. First, lower-frequency English words in each input segment are looked up in English–Belarusian dictionaries available in digital form, and the segment is translated N times (we use N=3) with the dictionary entries injected into the context and N times without them. Second, given the input segment and a pair of candidate translations, the model is prompted to merge both candidates into a single translation that would be as accurate as possible. At this stage, the context is augmented with the list of word forms from both candidates that are not attested in GrammarDB, the reference morphological database of Belarusian, and their suggested replacements from GrammarDB, ordered by weighted Levenshtein distance. Finally, given the input segment and the N merged translations after rule-based post-processing, the model is prompted to choose the best translation.

Description of your system highlights/te: Our system uses an agent-based translation optimization pipeline for the WMT26 shared task. For each input, the system collects candidate translations from multiple strong MT systems, together with listwise ranking scores and pairwise comparison results as evidence. The agent then makes an autonomous decision: it may directly select the best candidate, rewrite the translation by combining strengths from multiple candidates, or apply a more conservative editing strategy depending on the language direction, input characteristics, and observed candidate quality.  A separate judge module is used to evaluate the effect of each major step, including candidate selection, rewriting, and post-check correction. Based on this feedback, the system can adjust its subsequent strategy, such as choosing a different rewrite prompt, using a stricter or lighter post-editing policy, or changing the processing flow for specific language pairs. The agent evaluates translations using human-oriented criteria such as instruction adherence, structural alignment, faithfulness, terminology, grammar, register, fluency, and cleanliness. A final post-check stage detects severe issues such as truncation, broken structure, repetition, or clear mistranslation, and only applies minimal corrections when necessary.

Description of your system highlights/te: We describe the WPS-Qingqiu constrained-track submission to the WMT26 General Machine Translation shared task, registered as submission ID 45 in OCELoT. Our system covers all translation directions in the general translation task, and is based on Qwen3.5-9B. We first constructed instruction-translation data by using LLMs to generate instance-specific translation instructions and high-quality translations for each source sentence. In particular, to improve the diversity of translation instructions, we placed particular emphasis on instruction difficulty, task type, and expression style, and provided a rich set of candidate reference instructions. The model first underwent two-stage supervised fine-tuning: a large-scale, medium-quality SFT stage for broad capability acquisition, followed by a smaller-scale, high-quality SFT stage for refinement. Finally, we applied GRPO with a hybrid reward function combining LLM-as-a-judge feedback and rule-based signals. In our evaluation, the resulting model demonstrated strong instruction-based translation capability.

Description of your system highlights/te: We participated in the constrained (open-weight) track of the WMT 2026 General Machine Translation Task for the English-to-Japanese and Simplified Chinese-to-Japanese directions. Our system builds on Marco-MT-Algharb, a strong open-weight translation model from the previous WMT General MT task. We further fine-tuned this model to generate more natural Japanese translations. To this end, we constructed a Context-Aware Japanese Linguistic Acceptability dataset (CAJALA). During annotation, human annotators were shown multiple paraphrased variants of a segment within its document context and asked to select the most natural one. We then converted this dataset into parallel document pairs via back-translation and used them for preference learning with Direct Preference Optimization (DPO). We also trained the model to perform fill-in-the-middle (FIM) translation, in which the model reconstructs missing target-side segments of a document. At inference time, we first translated each test sample using Minimum Bayes Risk (MBR) decoding. We then applied FIM-style post-editing by selectively retranslating low-quality segments.

The submitted system uses the English-to-Korean profile and translates only the Korean-target subset of the blindset.
